clue.text: Is appearing after European legislator exhibits stress

indicators.note: says the word Is comes after the European legislator who exhibits

parts.note: an MP, Member of Parliament, makes laws
to have a quality is to exhibit it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Brussels lawmaker under pressure shows signs of strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is the stress laid on a word or point to mark its importance.

clue.text: Striker in game of soccer, say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: struck to light it
second meaning: a sporting contest, football being one example

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a centre-forward in a football game, but the striker is the thing you strike to make fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchstick lights by striking, and a fixture between two teams is also called a match.

clue.text: Parliamentary official missing first encouragement to cheer

indicators.note: the official's opening letter is left off

parts.note: a whip enforces party discipline in Parliament

explanation.surface: A party enforcer fails to rouse the benches to applause.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry before a hooray, as in three cheers, prompting the crowd to shout.

clue.text: Young boy embracing a learner in artistic gathering

indicators.note: the boy holds the other letters within his arms

parts.note: a son is a young male child
L is the learner plate abbreviation

explanation.surface: A lad hugs a student at an arts soirée.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is a fashionable assembly of writers, artists and thinkers at a host's home.

clue.text: Spare material certainly running short and not entirely lavish

indicators.note: the word is cut at its tail, losing its last letter

parts.note: sure as in 'sure, I will', meaning certainly

indicators.note: only part of the word is used, dropping its last letter

parts.note: plush means luxurious or lavish

explanation.surface: A tailor's leftover fabric is running low and not quite luxurious.
explanation.definitionFit: A surplus is an excess left over beyond what is needed.

clue.text: Record and listen in to end of debate

parts.note: to tap a phone is to listen in secretly

indicators.note: only the final letter of debate is used

explanation.surface: Someone secretly records and eavesdrops on the close of a debate.
explanation.definitionFit: To tape something is to make a recording of it, verb for verb.

clue.text: Approach in hybridising the quince?

indicators.note: crossing plants mixes their make-up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A gardener asks how one should go about crossing a quince with another fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A technique is a method or way of going about a task.

clue.text: Hobby? I'm covered in glue

indicators.note: the glue surrounds the other letters

parts.note: paste is a type of glue
I'M without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A modeller laments being smeared in adhesive by their pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastime is a leisure activity done for enjoyment, much like a hobby.

clue.text: Part of process seeing return of animals at home

indicators.note: the word for these animals is read backwards

parts.note: pets are domestic animals

explanation.surface: Bringing the family animals back is one stage of a routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is one stage in a sequence of actions.

clue.text: I cry unhappily during record — Sondheim?

indicators.note: the scrambled letters fall within the record

parts.note: a list is a written record

indicators.note: the letters of I cry are upset into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone weeps while listening to a Sondheim recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappily' rearranges I CRY to YRICI, which goes inside LIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Sondheim wrote the words for musicals, an example of a songwriter of lyrics, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Element of munitions disrupted her plans

indicators.note: her plans are thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An explosive part of an arms delivery wrecks a woman's schemes.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrapnel is the fragments of a shell or bomb scattered when it explodes.

clue.text: Times article probing unconventional leader, Greek leader

indicators.note: the two pieces push into the middle of the rearranged letters
the letters of leader are taken in an unusual order

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper item investigates a maverick politician, a Greek one.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter uses 'leader' twice on purpose: first as letters to shuffle, then in the definition. Times as X is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great was the Macedonian king who led the Greeks to conquer Persia.

clue.text: Nothing to secure a loose item in toolbox?

indicators.note: the word for nothing holds the letter a fast inside it

parts.note: nil means zero or nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing is there to fasten a stray item rattling in a toolbox.
explanation.definitionFit: Nails are small fixings that lie loose in a toolbox, ready to be hammered in.

clue.text: Second piano study to become broader

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
to read a subject at university is to study it

explanation.surface: A short piano study is meant to widen a student's range.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread is to extend or widen, covering more area.

clue.text: Expert Peg will secure good student

parts.note: a pro is an expert or professional

indicators.note: the peg holds the letter for good within itself

parts.note: a tee is the peg a golf ball sits on

explanation.surface: A skilled woman named Peg will take on a promising pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: Peg looks like a woman's name, but it is the golfer's tee.
explanation.definitionFit: A protégé is a pupil or younger person guided and supported by a mentor.

clue.text: Very serious item in the post about it's recalled

indicators.note: the whole combination is read backwards, as if called back
the postcard goes around the other letters

parts.note: a card is something sent by mail
IT'S without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A grave piece of mail is being withdrawn from circulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' acts on the whole assembly, not just on 'it's', so build the postcard wrapping first and then turn everything round.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are extreme and severe in their effect, hence very serious.

clue.text: Heads of state enterprises all but suppress later event

indicators.note: the first letter of each of the next two words
everything except the last letter is used

parts.note: to quell a rebellion is to suppress it

explanation.surface: State-owned businesses' bosses almost stifle what comes next.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequel is something that follows on from an earlier happening, such as a follow-up film.

clue.text: New star number presented by V and A

explanation.surface: A rising celebrity's figure is put on display at the V and A, the Victoria and Albert Museum in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for new, a nova is a star that suddenly flares into brightness.

clue.text: University employee of no practical use

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a lecturer or researcher at a university

explanation.walkthrough: The surface jibes at a useless lecturer; the two halves are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar teaching in higher education is a noun sense; the adjective means theoretical, without real consequence.

clue.text: Territorial Army containing such panic?

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words Territorial Army

explanation.surface: Can the reserve forces contain such fear?
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is sudden fear or anxiety about danger.

clue.text: Children matter

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a topic or subject under discussion

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like 'children are important', but the two words are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal language calls offspring someone's issue, and a point of debate is also an issue.

clue.text: Old soldier cheers, about to finish ongoing conflict

indicators.note: the old soldier wraps around the finish

parts.note: a vet is a veteran, a former soldier
an end is a finish
ta is British slang for thank you, as is cheers

explanation.surface: A veteran says thanks, about to settle a long-running feud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to finish' reads as 'nearly done', but 'about' is the wrapping signal and 'finish' is the piece inside the old soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged feud, often between families, carried on over years.

clue.text: Promote hot drink, on the way back

indicators.note: the pieces are read from right to left

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A café advertises hot drinks to customers heading home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way back' reads H + SUP backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To push a product is to promote or advertise it hard.

clue.text: Favouring endless support

indicators.note: the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a prop holds something up

explanation.surface: Someone is in favour of unlimited backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro as a preposition means in favour of, as in pros and cons.

clue.text: Put up with Winnie-the-Pooh?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the famous storybook teddy is an example of this animal

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Pooh is one example of the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate something is to bear it, and A. A. Milne's Pooh is a toy of that species.

clue.text: Firm opening of Magnificat — problem for Bach?

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: only the first letter of Magnificat is used

parts.note: a poser is a puzzling question or problem

explanation.surface: A tricky start to a Magnificat setting troubles Bach.
explanation.definitionFit: Bach is an example of someone who writes music, as the question mark signals.
